intro: Quality control analysts test products closely and judge whether they meet the standard, skills used in labs and manufacturing. The closest of the 25 careers below is inspecting, testing and sampling, with an 80% match, while aerospace engineering technologists are 78% matched with a BLS May 2025 median of $82,890.
why_it_works: Your work means running tests, reading results against specifications and stopping a batch when something is off. O*NET rates quality control analysis at 4 out of 5 for this job, and complex problem solving at 3.38. Engineering technology, chemistry and plant operations use the same analytical discipline. BLS reports this job within a broader group, so this page shows medians instead of percent changes.
tips: Quality Control Systems Managers earn $126,060 for their broader group, usually with a bachelor's degree.
Nuclear Power Reactor Operators earn $122,890 and are a 69% match without a new degree.
Learn statistical process control tools; operations analysis is one of your main gaps.

faq.q: What jobs can former quality control analysts do?
faq.a: The closest matches are inspectors, testers, sorters and samplers (80%), aerospace engineering technologists (78%) and Chemists (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Chemists earn a BLS May 2025 median of $91,240 but usually need a bachelor's degree in chemistry.

faq.q: Which jobs for quality control analysts pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Quality Control Systems Managers at $126,060, Nuclear Power Reactor Operators at $122,890 and power distributors and dispatchers at $106,730, according to BLS May 2025 data. Reactor and grid jobs train new operators on the job.

faq.q: Do quality control analysts need more education to switch?
faq.a: For some paths. 19 of the 25 matches need no more education than quality control analysts already have, including 7 of the top 10. In the closest match, 70% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, though chemistry and engineering roles usually need a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: What skills should quality control analysts learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing people, equipment selection, managing financial resources and operations analysis. Operations monitoring already rates 3.25 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so leading a quality team is the main step toward management.
